Mark Plays Nuitai

A blind playtest of the pygame demo by Mark, an invented professional playtester, thinking out loud. His notes follow the episode.

Mark Hey, welcome back. Episode 3. Last time I stopped by Maika's stall in the east half of the east forest, and I have not saved since the grove totem, so I'm carrying some risk. I've got 585 pule, a bag full of hide and pork, and one big question: where do I get a cup of water for Lanu's post here? My guess is the Sage in the grove hands them out. I also still owe Old Pono's wake a stew, and the day is going. So today: find a way back toward the grove, ask about cups, water this post, and look for the last two posts. Let me see where I'm standing.

Mark Okay, there's Maika's stall up top, the pond with the post at the left, mushrooms and boars scattered below. Kailo is the one on the right edge.

Mark Hm. Kailo isn't where I thought. I'm in this little pocket at the top right, boxed in by palms, and I tried every wall of it. Left, down, down again. Nothing. So how did I get in here last time? Let me think about the screen. The top row of the room is open grass. If I walk up the right edge... and there it is, a column on the far right that goes up to the top row. Okay, so the pocket has a door and it's the one I didn't try first. That's a lesson in this game's maps: the palms look like walls and then they leave one gap that you only find by checking every column.

Mark Writing that down: east edge of this room is a gap that shows on the narrator's list as an exit, but it's walled off from inside. Same as last episode, so it's a pattern, not a bug. I'll stay suspicious of those.

Mark Maika's stall. She's still there, I'm not buying anything yet, I want a cup of water first and I don't think she sells one. I'll go around the stall and head south, the long way back toward the grove. The west gap in this room is also walled off from inside, same thing.

Mark And here come the boars. One of them jumped me on the way down.

Mark Preemptive for them, I think. The turn bar opens with two boar faces on top. First thing is a parry: three blows, a Strong and two Mediums. I'll press each button at its own time, and the game is frozen between commands so I can read the numbers. Medium, Medium, Strong. Two parried, the Strong came in a hair late and Hina took 21. Fair.

Mark Fire boar and I have a water Kailo. Attack Strong gave me a 39 and filled my mana right up. Then the boar shifts to fire stance. So Flame Kick would be resisted. Hina took a 41 "Weak!" from its Flame Kick, so her flower stance is weak to fire. Noted: Hina's flower side takes extra from fire. That's kind of lovely, her two faiths have a body. I used Wave Guard, "Kailo stands guard over the party."

Mark I switched Kailo to Lelua and tried the combo, Pōhuehue, fire and flower, the beach vine. Notes first, I missed two of five because I used the wrong gaps between presses, then the spin and the crack. 95 and it still said "Resisted," because the boar had moved to fire. So the vine did 95 into a resist. That's a big number. "Wild Boar falls." One boar down. Combo is still the best thing in this game's fights.

Mark Two things I'm noting from that first fight. One, the game never tells you that a stance shift mid-fight changes what a hit will do. I wasted a combo's worth of vine into a resist. Two, the combo is still the best thing here. The spin at the end, up, right, down, left, with the crack on the last up, is a lovely little rhythm. It feels like winding a rope.

Mark Pork and a second Life Totem. I think those are the totem-in-your-pocket things, "they revive."

Mark Another pair of boars right after, this time we got the preemptive strike.

Mark Here I tried Scold again, since it did something unique last time. Hina went "out of breath" and the marks turn red, that's the debt. Kailo hit the other boar with Sauté, "Weak!", and then "Burn" came up, and the burn just did the rest. "Wild Boar B falls" on its own turn, nobody even touched it. I love that. Burn plus Scold is a real plan: Scold one, burn the other.

Mark Boar A hit Kailo with Flame Kick, "Resisted", no parry meter again. That's the third episode in a row where the elemental hits skip the meter. I'm going to treat it as designed, but the game has not once said it.

Mark Hina's Strong swings did 26 and 27. Kailo's Medium chain was 44 and 21. Two boars down and a "Thorn Strike" in the bag. That's an Element, I think, I'll learn it at the next menu. Also, "Pork" and Kukui. No pule from boars, which tells me they're only for items. Not a tough fight this time.

Mark Down to the north beach, and it's the same picture as last time: five Aghoys along the sand and a boardwalk maze with four straw-hat figures. I went in anyway. The idea is that the beach birds are dangerous in threes, so I'm not stopping there.

Mark Quick bag check before I forget. Four tabs in there, Ingredients, Medicine, Materials, Special, and an Elements one. Thorn Strike says "A thorny hit on one enemy," and the game tells me "KAILO can't learn this." That line is helpful, and it's the first time the game says why something won't go in. Osmose: "Enemy mana to an ally, +1." Neither of us could take it either. I'm still holding it. I wasted a good couple of minutes working out the tab order, and the cursor on the title bar looks the same as the cursor on the list, so I could not tell where I was.

Mark The straw-hat spirits are the Nuno sa Punso, the anthill spirits you say "tabi tabi po" to, and they jumped me again, preemptive. This is the good part. Nuno hardens against magic, but a combo ignores that. Pōhuehue did 218, then 231 on the second one. That's a huge jump from the 95 on the boar. The vine hits harder on a thing that takes a lot of regular damage, so I think the combo scales or the Nuno are weak to nature or fire somehow. Each fight pays 56 to 170 pule, which pays for the toll and then some. 840 now.

Mark Parry on the Nuno is a five-blow string, three Mediums and a Light. The trick I found: after each press the narrator recomputes the remaining time, so I press, read, press again. Two buttons only 0.08 seconds apart go together as one press with a gap. That works, but it's a lot of math for a blow-by-blow.

Mark "Seed of Vitality," two Toenails. And Kailo and Hina both say "STR up." Stats rise by use, so fighting here has a good feedback.

Mark The boardwalk had three more chests. A Smoke Bomb, 'Awa Tonic, and a Kagura Fan. I did not know there was an Equip page, so that was a nice find. The fan trades Vitality and Intelligence for Willpower and Luck, and the screen shows the new numbers in red and yellow before you commit, so I can tell at a glance it's a bad deal for Hina. That's a good comparison screen, and I'd say the game teaches equipment well.

Mark Another Nuno on the sand, and it dropped Bait. Bait. That has to be for fishing, which I need for the four fish in the stew. Pule is at 925 now.

Mark The long bridge. Nuno sa Tulay, the troll. Last episode I paid and was sent on. This time he wants 100 pule again going the other way, and I get three answers: pay, "I'm not paying that. This bridge is free for everyone to use.", or find another way around. I'm picking the second. Kailo is the kind of guy who stands his ground, and I'd said last time I wanted to see what a win gets me.

Mark "No? NO? Then I'll take it out of your hide!" Boss music, "Boss Battle 1". The first thing I notice is that he takes two turns before I get any.

Mark This fight went badly and I think I understand why. He shifts stance to spirit and his attacks stop giving me a parry meter at all, "lightning jumps to Hina," and then the great cyclone, a long run of hits on one target. Kailo went from full to zero in one cyclone, "Weak!" to wind, and then he's just lying there, "KO." Hina then has four turns in a row and no way to get him up.

Mark This is what I have to say about that. Life Totem is in Kailo's bag, and Hina can only reach her own bag, which holds one Noni Pulu. A knocked-out character's bag is locked. So the item meant to bring someone back can't be used by the person who is still standing, unless the person holding it is the one who is up. That is a real design problem, and I think it might be a bug, since a Life Totem is a consumable that is clearly for this case.

Mark I also tried Scold on the boss, since Scold is how I won fights this episode. "Nuno sa Tulay does not listen." And Hina went out of breath, in the red. So bosses are immune, which is fair, but the game wasn't clear about it. Heal is only 18 or 19 per cast, one mana each, and the cyclone does 30 to 60 a turn. I healed seven times in a row, no problem with that in itself, it just can't keep up with him.

Mark Hina fell. "Game Over."

Mark Okay. So that was a Game Over, and I want to be honest about what it cost. It dumped me on the title screen, I pressed Continue, and the game loaded the last save, the grove totem, from way back at the end of Episode 1. Everything since then, the pule, the Nuno loot, the Bait, the two fights, the chest items, is gone. 155 pule again. I had not saved in over an hour of play, so that's on me, but a Game Over that takes the whole session with it with no warning is harsh. I'd put that at large on the list, and a "Return to the totem?" line instead of a bare black screen would help.

Mark Silver lining: I'm at the grove, which is where I wanted to be. Let me find the Sage.

Mark There are three villagers here. A woman who says "I bring Lanu water from the spring every morning. It is hers anyway, but she likes being asked." A man who says "Shh. If you hold still, you can hear the rain coming before it comes." And an older man, "My knees hurt. I pray anyway. Lanu grew the knees, she can listen to them complain." Also "The temple is for Haka. The grove was here first." Nobody here is the Sage. The quest page says "The Lanu sage asked you to water the five posts in the grove. Water each one, then go back and tell the sage," and it's at 2 of 5. So the Sage should be here, and isn't.

Mark I tried the pond for a cup of water. Nope, the pond just heals the party, "Everyone is rested."

Mark Found something interesting though. The east door of the grove goes straight into the west side of Maika's glade, the lower left nook. So that's where the "west gap" I thought was walled off leads: it's a one-way shortcut from the grove, it's a nook with a chest and two red mushrooms. I fought one of the mushrooms. Hina Scold plus Kailo Sauté and the burn killed it. The chest said "It's empty," which means the game remembers a chest from the save, so the save has some flags older than my pack. Odd.

Mark South of the grove is the Crossroads Inn. Inside, the innkeeper only says "Aloha. You made it out of the woods. Every road on the island runs past my door." The shop sells Ginger Tea 30, Grilled Fish 50, Poi 30, Saimin 60, Egg 10, Pork 15, Ramen 50, Roast Pork 60. Grilled Fish for the stew? The recipe said Fish, not Grilled Fish.

Mark And a Traveler at a table answers three questions, and this is a good one. "A fallen friend can't eat, so food only helps the ones still on their feet. Haka's priests raise the fallen." So I think there's a way to raise a fallen ally and it belongs to Hina. That explains the boss fight and what I should have been doing: Hina's second stance, the Shaka one, likely holds the revive. I saw it had one element, "ShdGrd," and I did not look closely. That's a clue the game gives in a conversation, not a lesson, and I think it's good writing, but only if you thought to talk to a traveler at a table.

Mark West of the Crossroads there's a forest maze I hadn't seen, full of palms and round banyans, with boars, red mushrooms, and a spiky green thing in the corner. The first thing it teaches me is to treat every screen like a puzzle, because the exits are far from the entrances and at least two of the "pockets" are traps. I stood in a notch for a minute, just trying every direction. I ended up writing down the screen as a grid in my head and walking it that way, up, left, up, left, then down the long west side. It worked, and it's a lot of work for a player without a map.

Mark The Ōkole 'Iole fights are comfortable now. Scold, then Sauté, and it falls. Though I noticed the Scold sulk only lasts a few turns and sometimes ends before my own turn comes, so it's only worth it when Kailo is ahead of the mushroom in the order. Dropped: Frying Pan, Red Cap, Ti Leaf, Sauté from a boar.

Mark I opened the booklet. I want to say why. I could not find the Sage who gave me the posts quest, I had talked to every person in the grove and the inn, and I could not find a cup. I used a search for the words cup, post, sage and water, and it showed me more than I meant to read: it said saving happens only at an Akua totem, that praying at a totem also brings back the fallen, that you scoop fresh water from a river or pond by facing it and pressing A, and that a spring with sparkles over it only heals. So the cup is a scoop of water, taken from an ordinary pond, with a canteen. The grove pond has sparkles, so it only heals. I did not find the Sage there either, but now I know why I couldn't fill a cup: I was trying the wrong kind of water. I was looking for something to pick up, and the game wanted me to face the water and press A.

Mark And a chest on this new screen gave me an 'Awa Tonic, but every other chest on it is behind walls. The east and west gaps are sealed from inside again, that's four screens in a row with the same pattern. Time is nearly up, so I'm going to walk back to the grove and save.

Mark Back at the Crossroads. I tried the big lake east of the road, facing the water and pressing A like the booklet said. Nothing happens, no text, no sound, which makes sense if it's sea. That's one more thing the game could say out loud: "The water is salt." A silent button press is the most confusing answer a game can give.

Mark The garden at the inn had two Green Aghoys. They hit with a seven-light string, and I'm getting better at the rhythm of those: they come every 0.43 seconds, and two presses at a time is the way to do it. The Aghoys are the easiest fight in the screen once you know it. Combo again, 205 on the second one, and they fell together.

Mark Walked back to the grove and prayed at the totem. "The party kneels at the totem and tells the Akua all that has happened." Then the save screen: "Save your game?" with Yes on the left, then slot 1, then "Save over slot 1?" with No highlighted by default. I like that last one. That's a Game Over safeguard that does not exist anywhere else, it protects the save from a stray A press. Saved at 0:40 on the save clock, 245 pule.

Mark Hina's elements: Heal, "Heal one ally for 18 HP," and in her sun stance, ShdGrd, "Block 58% of shadow damage to an ally." So no revive in a stance, and the Traveler's line about the priests is flavor for the totem prayer. I was wrong about that, and it is a good reminder that what an NPC says in this game is not always a hint about a mechanic.

Mark One more Nuno on the road. It gave me a chest with Kapa Wraps. I compared them in Equip: Agility up 4, Luck up 2, but Strength down 7. Not for Kailo. The second Frying Pan I picked up is a worse version of the one he has, with less Vitality. I like that the same item name can have different numbers. But the list shows two Frying Pans with no way to tell them apart besides pressing the cursor over each one.

Mark The clock just rolled past the hour, so I'm going to stop and look back over what I saw, because a few screens are worth another look before I sign off.

Mark This is Hina's command menu in a fight: Attack, Scold, Element, Item, with the turn bar down the right side. It still reads clearly. You see the order, the portraits, and the HP bars with the mana marks under them.

Mark Kailo's Element list in his water stance, only Wave Guard. The stance name is the top line. I wish this screen said "Lelua: Sauté, Flame Kick" on the other side of the switch without making me spend the turn.

Mark The bag. Categories on the top bar, one description at the bottom. The cursor on the tab bar and the one on the list look the same, which is why I fumbled.

Mark The Elements tab, with colored corners that tell you what stance an Element suits.

Mark Giving Thorn Strike to a member. It says "A thorny hit on one enemy." The error is only on the second press, "KAILO can't learn this."

Mark The boardwalk maze, with the straw-hat spirits already on the move.

Mark Two of them closing in with an exclamation mark over one. Good telegraphing.

Mark Chests that are darker are opened, lighter ones are not. It's a nice quiet signal and I got it from noticing.

Mark The field menu has Equip, which I did not know about.

Mark Kailo's equip page, with the stat block and the stat arrows.

Mark The preview of the Kagura Fan on Hina: HP 170 to 140, Vitality 17 to 14, Intelligence 20 to 16, Willpower 14 to 17, Luck 8 to 10. Red is worse, yellow is better. That is a great way to show it.

Mark The long bridge, the troll at the bottom of it, the child's pier at the right, and the island with the white-and-red figure on the left that I still can't reach. That's my open question on this screen.

Mark The worst moment of the session: Kailo is knocked out, "KO," Hina at 19 of 190 and four turns in a row. The turn bar is all Hina.

Mark In flower stance she has Heal and that's it.

Mark And in sun stance, ShdGrd. Neither one brings anyone back.

Mark And the Game Over, plain white text on black. No "continue from the totem," no hint. It goes straight to the title screen, which is where I pressed A.

Mark The load screen says "1 The Pork Strikes Back", Lanu's Grove, 0:27, Nov 23 5:13 AM, 155 pule. That's the one I lost everything back to. The slot name is the title of the chapter I saved at the end of Episode 1, which is charming.

Mark The grove, a villager's text, and the pond with sparkles.

Mark The Info page. Quests, Bestiary, Glossary, Lore, Records, with a clock that says 0:28 and 433 steps, and "30th of Kau."

Mark "The Lanu sage asked you to water the five posts in the grove. Water each one, then go back and tell the sage." Posts 2 of 5. A really clear quest log entry, and still I couldn't find the sage.

Mark The nook off the grove, the same screen as Maika's glade, seen from its west door.

Mark After I cleared one of the mushrooms. The chest is "empty," because the game remembers a chest I opened last time but I lost the item.

Mark The grove from the east door.

Mark The Crossroads Inn and the road, with the garden of purple taro and two Green Aghoys.

Mark Inside the inn: the innkeeper, the cook at the pot with the leaf crown, a traveler at a table, crates of fish, greens and tomatoes in the corner, and three beds.

Mark The shop's Sell tab and the "Hot and fresh. The cook starts at dawn." line.

Mark The shop: Ginger Tea 30, Grilled Fish 50, Poi 30, Saimin 60, Egg 10, Pork 15, Ramen 50, Roast Pork 60, and I'm "Owned: 0" on Poi.

Mark The west maze, and a good look at how hard it is to read: palms and banyans are the same color as the grass.

Mark And the maze under it, with four chests I can see and three I can't reach. The lake in the corner has the same problem. This screen shows chests and water behind walls that I cannot get to, which is a lot of teasing.

Mark The same screen after I cleared the mushroom, and Kailo up in the top row.

Mark The first maze again, from the Crossroads side.

Mark The Crossroads, with the inn, the garden and the lake.

Mark The grove at the end. Kailo is by the pond and the totem is bottom right.

Mark "Saved to slot 1." 0:40, 245 pule.

Mark Hina's Element page: Heal.

Mark ShdGrd: "Block 58% of shadow damage to an ally".

Mark The Nuno with the chest in the little corridor.

Mark The second Frying Pan: HP 130 to 100 and Luck 8 to 10.

Mark Kapa Wraps: Agility up, Strength down.

Mark The Lore page with its six categories.

Mark "People. 6 of 13." The game tells you how much is left to find, which I love.

Mark Ama: "an old fisherman of Kulāiwi who works on the village docks and keeps a bait and tackle shop. He learned boatbuilding as an apprentice of KAILO's father, who built half the boats in the harbor. His name means the outrigger float that..." So Kailo's father was a boatbuilder.

Mark And Ulu: "the chief of Kulāiwi. His name means breadfruit, the tree that feeds a village." The names are all things, a float, a fruit. I love that about this world, and it tells me the author knows Hawaiian.

Mark Okay. That's an hour. I saved at the grove, I'm back where I want to be, and I still need a cup of water and a way to the Sage and the Great Boar. Thanks for watching. A good place to stop. Next time I want to scoop water at a real pond and water the post in the glade, find the Sage, and try the troll again with proper preparation.

End of episode

What happened

Start: Kulāiwi Forest, Maika's glade (east half of the east forest), Kailo boxed in a pocket at the top right (14,4). Found the way out: the pocket's open side is the right-hand column up to the top row; the other three sides are palms. Walked around Maika's stall and south.

Fights, in order:

1. Wild Boar (ambushed by it, parry of Medium, Medium, Strong; two parried, Strong a hair late, Hina took 21). Pōhuehue combo: 95, "Resisted" (boar had shifted to fire stance). Drops: Pork, Life Totem.

2. Two Wild Boars (preemptive strike). Hina Scold on A (sulking); Sauté on B ("Weak!", Burn); B died of the burn; Hina's Strong swings 26 and 27 finished A. Drops: Thorn Strike, Kukui. No pule from boars.

3. Nuno sa Punso on the north-beach boardwalk (preemptive): Pōhuehue 218, then another Nuno, 231. Drops: Nuno Toenail (x2), Seed of Vitality, Bait. Pule 585 to 925 (this was before the loss).

4. Nuno sa Punso ahead of the sand (Nuno, Pōhuehue 236).

5. Chests: Smoke Bomb, Kagura Fan, 'Awa Tonic.

6. Nuno sa Tulay, the troll on the long bridge (refused the toll). Boss. Went to spirit stance; lightning and "great cyclone" attacks with no parry meter; Kailo KO in one cyclone, Hina alone for several turns, Scold failed ("does not listen"), Heal only 18 per cast. Hina fell. Game Over.

7. Title screen, Continue, slot 1 loaded: back at the grove totem with 155 pule and the Episode 1 bag (everything from Episode 2 and the first half of this one gone).

8. Talked to the three villagers in the grove (no Sage found), tried the pond (heals), found the grove's east door leads into the west nook of Maika's glade (chest said "It's empty"), fought one 'Ōkole 'Iole there (Scold plus Sauté; dropped Kukui Nut).

9. Crossroads Inn: innkeeper (Stay the night / Buy food / Talk / Leave), shop list, the cook (three questions, known), a Traveler (three questions), and a man at the table.

10. West maze (west of the Crossroads): a Wild Boar ambush on the way (burned to death with Sauté, dropped Sauté), another 'Ōkole 'Iole (dropped Red Cap, Frying Pan), the next screen south with four chests; one reachable ('Awa Tonic), a third 'Ōkole 'Iole (dropped Ti Leaf), another Wild Boar (Boar Hide).

11. Crossroads garden: two Green Aghoys (Kukui, Green Wing; pule 155 to 245). Nuno sa Punso with the chest (Kapa Wraps).

12. Walked to the grove and saved in slot 1 (0:40 on the save clock, 245 pule) at the 50:56 mark.

13. Read Info, Lore, People (6 of 13); Ama and Ulu entries.

Ended at 60:07, in Kulāiwi Forest at the Crossroads, standing near the Inn door, Kailo 130/130, Hina 89/160 (not rested since the save). Last save: grove totem, slot 1.

Stuck and confusing

1. Start of the episode: Kailo stood at the top right of Maika's glade. Screen: a pocket of palms, the narrator said "Kailo leads, facing down, toward something solid" every way he tried (down, right, left, down again). He pressed down, right, down, left several times. The exit (the right-hand column up to the top row) was never mentioned.

2. Narrator lists "Open edges, to another area" for gaps that cannot be reached from inside (east and west gaps in Maika's glade, west and east gaps of the next maze). Pressing toward them did nothing; the narrator says "solid". That is four screens in a row.

3. The Game Over: after the boss the screen was plain white text on black. A press went to the title. Continue went to the Episode 1 save (155 pule, 0:27). Nothing said what would happen or that progress would be lost. (Large.)

4. The bag: Life Totem sat in Kailo's bag; when Kailo was knocked out, Hina's Item menu showed only her own bag (one Noni Pulu). No way to use it. The narrator showed "Highlighted: Noni Pulu x1" only.

5. Scold on the troll (Nuno sa Tulay): the mash worked, but the text said "Nuno sa Tulay does not listen." and Hina went out of breath. Nothing earlier tells the player bosses ignore Scold.

6. The troll's spirit stance attacks had no parry meter ("lightning jumps to Hina," "great cyclone"), hit for 30 to 60 per turn, and the "Weak!" popped on Kailo. The narrator said "Pops up over Hina: 30". Same pattern as the Resisted/Weak! blows: no meter, never explained.

7. Combo access: "press right on the commands" only works when the partner is next to you on the turn bar; the narrator does not say why Combo is greyed out ("Highlighted: Combo (grayed out)") and I pressed right on the wrong turn several times.

8. Light attack chain in the troll fight: pressing c,c,c as three keys in one press did nothing (the controller allows two keys). Not a game issue, a controller one, but the game's attack bar still said "Waiting on a command" and I spent turns on tiny attacks that burned turn slots.

9. The bag's tab bar: pressing right while the hook was on the page did nothing; I had to press up to put the hook on the tab bar. The hook looks the same on both. I got to the Elements tab by pressing right one at a time.

10. Giving an Element: the "can't learn this" message only shows on the screen, the narrator said nothing ("HEARD:" empty, a dull bump sound).

11. The Sage never appeared. The quest page says "The Lanu sage asked you to water the five posts in the grove." All three grove villagers say flavor lines and none offer the quest. Posts 2 of 5. The post in the grove shows a cup of water.

12. Pressing A at the sea at the Crossroads did nothing, no text, no sound.

13. The save said "Saved to slot 1" at 0:40, but the first slot name "The Pork Strikes Back" did not change.

14. The field menu Element page: pressing R (e) did nothing while Hina's tutorial text was waiting; I had to press z several times before B would close it. The menu shows the tutorial lines again each time ("See the rows?" and "Row 2 is twice as strong as row 1").

15. The south gap in the west maze: the narrator listed it as "its nearest gap 3 down" while Kailo stood in a pocket with a palm below; I needed a grid solver to find the way (left, up, around).

16. The narrator's turn-order line sometimes shows the same character 3 or 4 times in a row (Hina, Hina, Hina), which looks like extra turns. Using a light attack seemed to use up one of them; using a Heal did not.

17. "Wild Boar curls up" and "Wild Boar is out of breath!" appeared in the same stretch; I cannot tell whether sleeping and being out of breath are the same state.

18. Pule: boars drop none, Nuno pay 56 to 170, the Aghoys 90. After the loss, the displayed pule was 155.

Design notes

1. The Pōhuehue combo is the best thing in the game: three-part input (notes, a spin, a crack), 95 to 236 damage, and it scales with enemy stance. Praise. Keep.

2. The Game Over sends the player back to a save hours old with no warning and no choice. Large.

3. A knocked-out character's bag is locked, so Life Totem is unusable in the situation it exists for. The Traveler's line about priests raising the fallen is not backed by an element. Large.

4. Bosses ignore Scold with no hint; Scold costs the whole mana bar and sends the character into debt. Medium.

5. The troll's spirit-stance attacks have no parry meter and hit for more than anything else. The fight is a gear check that is not signposted. Large.

6. Preview of equipment stats with red/yellow arrows is excellent. Praise. Small.

7. "Posts 2 of 5" with a progress bar and the quest giver's name is a great quest log. Praise. The Sage being unfindable makes it a trap. Medium.

8. Lore page "People, 6 of 13" gives a clear goal and the Ama and Ulu entries add real world detail (names that mean things). Praise.

9. The "Save over slot 1?" prompt defaults to No. Praise. Small.

10. The map screens have palms and banyans colored like grass; many pockets are traps and the exits sealed. A maze that needs a grid solver is too hard to read. Medium.

11. Nuno sa Punso are great enemies: they telegraph, they cluster, they pay well, and the combo wins fights in one go. Praise.

12. Turn order bar: using cheap actions to shift the order is a deep idea that is never taught. Medium (design depth, not a bug).

13. The Equip menu, Mastery tab, and Config exist but were never mentioned. Small.

14. Scold sulk lasts a few turns and can expire before the player's next turn. Small.

15. Saved loot the player cannot hold (a chest that says "It's empty" because of a save flag) after a reload is confusing. Small.

Story and characters

Little new story this episode. The Sage is missing from the grove. The Traveler's lines and Ama and Ulu's lore entries add: Ama is an old fisherman and bait and tackle shopkeeper who apprenticed under Kailo's father, a boatbuilder who built half the boats in the harbor; Ulu is the chief and his name means breadfruit. Hina's lines in the field menu repeat her teaching ("Row 2 is twice as strong as row 1", "Put what you use most where you can pay for it. I won't say it twice."). The innkeeper: "Aloha. You made it out of the woods. Every road on the island runs past my door." Grove villagers: "I bring Lanu water from the spring every morning. It is hers anyway, but she likes being asked." "Shh. If you hold still, you can hear the rain coming before it comes." "The temple is for Haka. The grove was here first." Nuno sa Tulay: "No? NO? Then I'll take it out of your hide!" Hina is still the best written. Kailo is a quiet practical cook. Maika still sells things from her stall.

Predictions

- Open: the island won't stay untouched past the opening.

- Open: Kailo will follow his dad or Hina off the island. The Ama entry makes the boat link stronger: his father built boats, so the way off the island is probably a boat.

- Open: Old Pono's death and the Callers of Makua will connect.

- Open: the stew is the first real recipe, cooked at Noelani's fire.

- Open: the Great Boar is Lanu's; the dry posts tie to it.

- Open: the south's "take Mana from a beaten champion" becomes a villain's idea.

- Open: the giant moth on the mountain is real and a boss.

- Wrong (new): "the east-edge gaps are entrances from screens not yet reached." The gap in Maika's glade west door leads to the grove nook, so that one was a one-way entrance from outside. The others, still sealed.

- Wrong: "Lanu's cups come from the Sage." The Sage was not in the grove; the booklet says water is scooped from a pond; I did not complete it.

- Wrong (new): the Life Totem is how the party revives in a fight. It could not be used.

- Wrong (new): "Haka's priests raise the fallen" meant Hina had a revive. She doesn't; it's a totem prayer.

- Right: Heal All belongs on Hina's second row (not tested).

- Right: Hina's flower side takes extra from fire ("Weak!" 41, 15).

- Right: bosses are the next step up: the troll fight is a boss.

- New open: Kagura Fan was meant for someone else (maybe Melia or a later character).

The booklet

Opened once, at about the 41 minute mark. Why: I could not find the Lanu sage who gives the posts quest and I had no cup of water; I had talked to the three grove villagers, tried the pond, the inn, the cook and the traveler. What I looked up: the words "cup", "post", "sage", "water". It helped: it told me fresh water is scooped from a river or pond by facing it and pressing A (a spring with sparkles only heals), and that totems revive and save. It also showed me more than I asked for (save rules, tools, swimming, fishing, the B button's preemptive swing) because the search matched several lines; I did not read the rest. Where it disagreed with the game: the booklet says praying at a totem brings back the fallen, which the in-game totem line ("tells the Akua all that has happened") does not say. I did not find a "canteen" in the bag, so I still cannot do what the booklet says.

Review so far

Nuitai wants to be a Chrono Cross style RPG where timing, rhythm and stance choices matter in every fight, in a world with Polynesian and Southeast Asian color and a cooking theme. What works: the combo is a joy; the turn bar makes tempo a real resource; the Nuno and the mushrooms teach "find the rule" fights; the writing is warm and specific; the Info and Lore pages are clear. What does not: the world map is hard to read (grass-colored walls, sealed exits), the boss fight punishes without teaching, and Game Over takes hours of progress back to the last save with no warning. I would not yet recommend it to a general player; I would to someone who likes systems and writing and is willing to save often at totems. With a clearer boss warning, a gentler Game Over, a way to use the Life Totem, and a visible Sage I'd say yes.

My notes for next time

Haka's priests raise the fallen."), three grove villagers (water from the spring each morning, the rain, the temple and the grove), Maika (stall in the glade), the Nuno sa Tulay troll (bridge, toll 100 pule, boss if you refuse), Ama (old fisherman, bait and tackle, taught by Kailo's father the boatbuilder), Ulu (chief, breadfruit).

- Places: the grove's east door goes into the west nook of Maika's glade. The grove's south gap leads to the Crossroads Inn; west of the Inn is a forest maze (boars, mushrooms, a spiky plant) and south of that a maze with four chests (one reachable, 'Awa Tonic). East of the Crossroads is a lake (sea).

- Rules: the Combo needs both at 7 mana and side by side on the turn bar, press right on the command menu, notes (up, tab, up, tab, z at 1.18, +0.25 each), then a spin (up, right, down, left, repeating, ending up then z). Bosses ignore Scold. Spirit-stance attacks have no parry meter. A knocked-out character's bag is locked. Save only at a totem; Game Over loads the last save.

- Theories: boats are the way off the island; the Great Boar and the dry posts connect; cups are scooped water.

- Do next: scoop water at a pond and water the post in Maika's glade (needs a canteen?), find the Sage and the other two posts, find the hunters' lodge, go back to the troll with a stronger party and a plan (Wave Guard, Heal, light parries), and save before.

Checked (by the session that ran the episode)

- The Sage was in the grove the whole time and is not behind any story flag: he stands at the left of the post, always there day and night, and talks to anyone (his first line is "Lanu's grove. Keep your voice down, the trees are listening. Ask if you want to know something."). Mark talked to the other two people, the woman and the old man, and counted the woman's two lines as two people. His line after five posts is a gift (Hina's Revive); short of five he says how many are left. The screenshot at the start of the grove visit shows him. An AI misreading, not a game problem. Not passed on.

- Game Over going back to the last save is ruled: a GAME OVER screen, then the title, where the player loads the last save and anything since is lost, Final Fantasy VI style (Frankie, 10/24; game/answers.md). The booklet says to pray at a totem and save before a big fight. A Game Over is expected now and then and is not a problem by itself (Frankie, 11/3). He knew at the start of the episode that he had not saved since Episode 1's totem. Not passed on.

- Hina could not use Kailo's Life Totem: ruled. Each fighter carries their own battle bag and only the acting member's bag can be used in a fight (Frankie, 11/12), and the booklet's Battle Bags page and the Item command both say so. The totem was in Kailo's bag. Not passed on.

- Nuno sa Tulay ignoring Scold is ruled: bosses are never scolded or charmed (Frankie, 10/25), and the game does say "does not listen". Scold going into mana debt is ruled too. Not passed on.

- The troll's spirit attacks with no parry meter: ruled and taught. Only plain strokes are parried, never elements or Skills (Frankie, 10/30), and the booklet's Parrying page says so in so many words. Third episode in a row with the same note (already on the list for Kevin). Beating the troll is a puzzle, and he is the optional bridge boss with 700 HP (game/answers.md). Not passed on.

- Exits that look open but are sealed: real in the data and already known from Episodes 1 and 2. Maika's glade is split into three walled pieces: the main room, a pocket holding its two east gaps, and a west nook with the chest, which is reached only from the grove's east door. Checked by tracing the room's grid. Whether this is wanted is Frankie's call, not new here. The start pocket Kailo woke in has an open side (the right-hand column), as he found.

- The chest in the west nook saying "It's empty" is not a save fault: it was opened in Episode 1 (the memory says "chest taken"), and the flag is on the Episode 1 save he loaded.

- The save slot's name "The Pork Strikes Back" not changing is by design: the name is the chapter, and it changes only after the Great Boar falls.

- Pressing A at the sea doing nothing, the narrator saying nothing for the "can't learn this" message, c,c,c in one press, and the turn-order line repeating a name are the tool or the narrator, not the game. The hook looking the same on the page and on the tab bar and the greyed Combo giving no reason are small, unchecked, and not passed on.

- Wild Boar "curls up" (asleep) and "out of breath" (mana debt) are two different states, not one.

- New for Kevin rather than Frankie, if a player really cannot tell: after a Game Over the screen is plain white text on black with no "return to the last save" line. This is as ruled, so only the wording could be Frankie's call.

- His money: the facts sheet says 330 pule at the end, not the 245 in his notes (he saved at 245). His memory uses the facts sheet for where the game stands, and the save is 245.

- The Game Over wiped the whole of Episode 2 and the first half of this one from the game: the save he loaded is Episode 1's (155 pule). In his own memory it all still happened, so he remembers the Nuno sa Punso, the Aghoys, the toll and the fights as things that happened, but the game does not have them (the loot, the elements Episode 2 found, the pule). Both are in his memory file.
